key_insight: In simply-connected analytic domains, a nontrivial rigidly rotating vortex patch forces the outer boundary to be a centered disk, while small boundary deformations can still support quasi-periodic patch motions for most inner radii.
engineering_relevance: These results clarify when geometry preserves or destroys coherent vortex structures, which is useful for flow control, reduced-order modeling, and understanding vortical persistence in bounded fluids.
method: Use a rotating-frame reformulation of the 2D Euler equations.
Apply harmonic unique continuation and generalized Schwarz reflection across analytic boundary arcs.
Construct quasi-periodic patch solutions perturbatively for domains near the unit disk.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rigorous analytical theorems and constructive existence results, including rigidity proofs and a perturbative solution family for most values of the inner radius.
watch_item: The quasi-periodic construction is perturbative and depends on domains being small deformations of the disk with real-analytic boundaries, so it may not extend to strongly non-radial geometries.
paper_title: Geometric effects on the persistence of patch structures for 2D Euler equations in simply-connected bounded domains
